title: Root a $50 BIUFRAME into a home dashboard
summary: Wes Bos documented a guarded ADB-and-SuperSU workflow that identifies the board, verifies a full backup, removes vendor/FOTA apps, updates the browser stack and turns the frame into a USB-powered kiosk.
outcome: A rooted touch display running a modern web dashboard. Independent photos and videos from Philip Ideson and Deepak show the broader frame-dashboard idea reproduced, although their exact boards are undisclosed.

design_ideas.title: Family calendar and chores hub
design_ideas.description: Run a responsive browser dashboard with the next appointments, weather and chores. A computer or server supplies authenticated data; a matching rooted frame displays it.

design_ideas.title: AI briefing panel
design_ideas.description: Render a short daily briefing as a web page. Keep AI generation and account credentials on a trusted backend; expose only the finished display content to the frame.

warnings: The same Amazon listing now ships materially different boards; confirm the Rockchip RK3126 fingerprint and partition layout before using this guide.
The Android 6 security base is obsolete. Keep the frame on an isolated network and do not use primary accounts.
The community replications do not disclose their board identity, so they do not establish compatibility for every frame sold under the listing.

title: Reclaim the Allwinner photo frame hiding under the same listing
summary: A separate guide covers the Allwinner A33 PF1007L now commonly shipped under the BIUFRAME listing, with identity-dependent paths through stock ADB, an AiMOR-mediated temporary root, FEL or a guarded boot patch.
outcome: A local kiosk or dashboard on the Allwinner frame without applying the incompatible Rockchip instructions.

design_ideas.title: Room information display
design_ideas.description: Use the board-specific kiosk path to show an HTML calendar, weather or household page. Confirm the firmware and browser capability first; this is separate from the Rockchip frame design.

warnings: Do not use the Synergy 10X1/Rockchip guide on this board. Confirm model string, SoC, USB IDs, fingerprint and partitions first.
Require a byte-verified backup before any write and stop on every identity or hash mismatch.
Some units expose unauthenticated root ADB or a vendor remote-root path; isolate them from untrusted networks.

title: Replace Alexa with Muse on an Echo Show 5
summary: Hey Muse builds on TECHO5 to pair an unlocked Echo Show with Meta's Muse app, run a local Hey Muse wake word and speak answers through a built-in or cloud voice.
outcome: A repurposed smart display that boots a small Linux image and acts as a Muse voice-and-screen body without Alexa or Amazon cloud services.
warnings: The public release image and physical test cover one Echo Show 5 2nd gen only. The Dot shown in the social clip is explicitly untested by this repository.
Unlocking and flashing can brick the device; preserve TECHO5 backups, TWRP and restore material.
Wake-word detection is local, but up to 60 seconds of post-wake audio is uploaded to and retained by Muse; cloud TTS also receives answer text.

title: Turn three Amazon speakers into local Assist satellites
exact_models: Echo Dot 3 D9N29T / donut / Fire OS 6574.1
Echo Dot 2 RS03QR / biscuit / Fire OS 6574.1
summary: Echo Dot Assist preserves Amazon's microphone and wake-word stack while replacing Alexa with a local Home Assistant ESPHome/Wyoming daemon on three tightly pinned hardware and firmware combinations.
outcome: Local wake-word, voice capture and Home Assistant Assist on otherwise cloud-bound Echo speakers.
warnings: The author labels the project vibecoded and unaudited. Bootloader and system writes can brick the speaker.
Support is exact-model and exact-firmware only; Dot 3 refresh C78MP8 and Dot-with-clock 36EBT3 are excluded.
Download stock images and rehearse the documented TWRP/fallback restore path before writing.

title: Reclaim a Lenovo Smart Clock 2 without permanent flashing
summary: smartclock2tool uses a runtime-only kernel exploit for temporary root, SSH and Wi-Fi ADB; Helios adds a local Home Assistant dashboard, wake word and Music Assistant interface.
outcome: A local smart display that returns to stock after a power cycle and avoids bootloader or partition writes.
warnings: Validated on one exact build; the exploit can kernel-panic and is not evidence for other Smart Clock firmware.
While active, SELinux is permissive and ADB authentication is disabled. Isolate the clock and disable ADB outside setup.
Power cycling removes root and ADB, which is recovery—not proof that every failure mode is harmless.

title: Replace Roborock cloud services with a local server
summary: local_roborock_server recreates the vacuum's HTTPS and MQTT cloud endpoints with DNS and certificate onboarding, without rooting or writing custom firmware.
outcome: A Roborock S8 controlled through a fully local server, with an exact firmware/certificate combination recorded in the compatibility matrix.
warnings: Firmware and certificate combinations materially change compatibility; use the tested-vacuum matrix, not the brand name.
Several newer Q-series variants are explicitly unsupported.
DNS and certificate onboarding affect network trust; isolate and audit the local service.

title: Run LG ThinQ appliances against a local cloud emulator
summary: rethink emulates LG ThinQ's cloud locally and translates appliance traffic to MQTT/Home Assistant, with optional bridge mode for retaining the official app.
outcome: Local status and control for specific documented ThinQ models without modifying appliance firmware.
warnings: Support levels differ by exact ThinQ model token; do not generalize across all LG appliances.
Provisioning and a local cloud emulator create a network-security surface that must be isolated and maintained.
Remote HVAC control should retain manufacturer limits and physical supervision.

title: Speak Haier's encrypted local AC protocol
summary: haismart-local implements the encrypted TCP/56800 protocol and records a hardware-confirmed combination down to product code, Wi-Fi module and firmware.
outcome: Local power, mode, setpoint, fan, vane, self-clean and energy readings after a one-time cloud login retrieves the device key.
warnings: The model sticker alone is insufficient; match product code, U+ ID, module and firmware.
The one-time cloud login obtains a local key but does not automatically disable vendor cloud access.
Keep HVAC protections authoritative and verify every write with device readback.

title: Replace a Rainy 75 Pro keyboard's firmware with ZMK
summary: A hardware-verified ZMK port covers the keyboard's USB, BLE, 83-key matrix and RGB functions while documenting the stock image and hardware recovery route.
outcome: An open keyboard firmware replacing the vendor image on verified ANSI and ISO boards.
warnings: The proprietary 2.4 GHz dongle mode is not ported; only USB and BLE are supported.
Keep a stock image. A failed OTA may require a Telink burning board on SWS pads.
Use releases from the repository; the maintainer warns that third-party firmware downloads may be malware.

title: Use AirPods features without Apple's software stack
summary: LibrePods reverse-engineers the AirPods protocol to expose noise modes, battery and ear detection on Android and Linux without changing earbud firmware.
outcome: A cross-platform protocol client for core AirPods controls and telemetry outside Apple's ecosystem.
warnings: Protocol behavior changes with earbud firmware; 7A305 evidence is not a promise for later releases.
Advanced Android integrations may require root, Xposed or specific OS builds.
Do not represent ear-detection or hearing-related telemetry as medical data.

title: Reclaim an abandoned Sengled hub as a Zigbee coordinator
summary: sengled-hub-reclaim converts first- and second-generation hubs into local EZSP v7 Zigbee coordinators with a dry-run gate, complete backup and retained recovery bank.
outcome: A cloud-independent Zigbee coordinator built from a discontinued hub.
warnings: Third-generation Sengled hubs are explicitly incompatible.
The release is destructive and has a small test population; supervise flashing even though Bank1 is retained.
Run the compatibility dry-run and verify the full backup before any Bank2 write.

title: Install open firmware on a GeekMagic pixel display
summary: GeekMagic Open Firmware replaces the stock image over OTA or USB-TTL and includes a rescue access point after repeated boot failures.
outcome: A fully open small pixel display with local customization and a documented recovery path.
warnings: The rescue access point is unauthenticated; do not leave it exposed.
EEPROM secret storage is obfuscation, not encryption.
Confirm the exact ESP8266/ST7789 board before using an image.

title: Add an open local stack to an Anycubic Kobra 3
summary: Rinkhals retains the stock printer UI and features while adding SSH, Mainsail, Fluidd, Moonraker and installable local apps.
outcome: A locally extensible 3D printer that keeps the vendor interface while exposing the open Klipper ecosystem.
warnings: Kobra X is explicitly unsupported; match the model and stock firmware table.
Change the documented default root password and isolate the printer before enabling network services.
Firmware changes affect heaters and motion. Re-test thermal cutoffs and supervise first prints.

title: Patch a Xiaomi smart speaker for local audio services
summary: xiaoai-patch modifies the inactive root filesystem to add MPD, Snapcast, Shairport, Squeezelite, Whisper and Home Assistant integrations.
outcome: A vendor smart speaker repurposed as a flexible local network audio endpoint.
warnings: Have TTL/U-Boot recovery available before writing the inactive root filesystem.
Encrypted DER-rootfs models such as LX05 and L15A must not be flashed with this path.
The Linux build and model-specific firmware requirements make this an expert-level modification.

title: Take a CM4 Vestaboard fully offline
summary: vestaboard-offline documents the board's Yocto/CM4 stack and RS485 flap protocol, then replaces its vendor-cloud dependency with a local controller.
outcome: A physical split-flap display controlled locally after root/SSH access and vendor-cloud removal.
warnings: The local controller binds to 0.0.0.0:7000 without documented authentication; add authentication or isolate the LAN.
The workflow requires root/SSH and disables the vendor cloud.
Confirm the CM4/A-B image layout before modifying any Vestaboard revision.

title: Replace the runtime on an Ulanzi TC002 Pixbar
device_name: Ulanzi Pixbar Smart Pixel Clock II
summary: tc002-customisation documents stock root ADB and HTTP behavior, a reversible /tmp runtime and an optional replacement runtime written only after device fingerprinting and backup verification.
outcome: A locally controlled 52x16 pixel display with an incremental path from reversible experiment to persistent replacement.
warnings: The stock device exposes unauthenticated control, root ADB and weak credential storage; use an isolated IoT network.
Run the reversible in-place mode first and preserve a verified res-partition backup before flashing.
Replacement runtime is beta-quality and the repository has no declared license.

title: Replace an ACiQ mini-split's Wi-Fi module with ESPHome
summary: The project decodes the stock module's 115200 8N1 UART bus and provides an ESPHome takeover with hardware-proven commands, ACKs, heartbeat and a safer receive-only listener mode.
outcome: Cloud-free mini-split telemetry and control through an ESP32 connected to the exact CN-16 module bus.
warnings: Stock-dongle listener and ESP32 takeover configurations are mutually exclusive; two push-pull transmitters can damage hardware.
The bus is 5 V logic and requires the documented level shifting; wire colors are nonstandard.
Exact-model only: other ACiQ ducted systems use a different XYE/RS-485 project.

title: Control a Tapo P110 with no cloud account
summary: tapo-local reimplements the app's SPAKE2+ handshake and AES-128-CCM protocol for local Wi-Fi and BLE relay, metering, protection and history access.
outcome: Cloud-free smart-plug control and energy data without flashing the sealed device.
warnings: The local key derives from the MAC plus a fixed app secret; keep the plug on a trusted network segment.
This is a mains relay. Respect load ratings and constrain automations.
The repository does not publish a firmware-flash path; this is protocol control, not custom firmware.

title: Control firmware-qualified Orbit B-Hyve timers over BLE
device_name: Orbit B-Hyve hose timers and XD controllers
summary: orbit-bhyve-ble obtains per-device AES keys once, then uses local BLE with a hardware-and-firmware compatibility matrix rather than claiming blanket brand support.
outcome: Local watering status and actuation for six tested model/firmware combinations after one cloud-assisted key retrieval.
warnings: Do not accept vendor firmware updates blindly; encryption and packet trailers may change.
HT25A-0001 has a hardware-confirmed STOP/duration bug and requires the project's alternate stop command and host timer.
Firmware recovery is verified only for HT25-0000 fw0085; other proxy recovery paths remain experimental.

title: Replace QuietCool attic-fan firmware with ESPHome
summary: quietcool-esphome-native installs over the controller's BLE OTA and preserves fan control, Smart Mode, timers, buttons, LEDs and OEM BLE app control with stock-restore and recovery paths.
outcome: Local Home Assistant control of an exact attic-fan controller with end-to-end hardware testing and layered recovery.
warnings: Preserve thermal and watchdog cutoffs; software control is not a safety system.
Check the exact controller identity before OTA and keep the stock-restore image available.
OEM historical analytics and AirControl features are not preserved.

title: Proxy a LifeBreath HRV control bus with ESPHome
summary: An ESP32-S3 sits as a protocol-aware proxy on the proprietary three-wire open-collector bus, preserving the original wall panel and timers while adding local Home Assistant control.
outcome: Bidirectional local control and telemetry without discarding the appliance's original controls.
warnings: Only the exact RNC6-ES/DXPL-03 combination is tested.
The low-voltage bus is inside a 120 V appliance and installation requires cutting a wire; switch off the breaker before opening.
Never connect 5 V directly to an ESP32 GPIO or hard-drive the open-collector line.

title: Control a Charnwood stove locally with OpenWood
summary: OpenWood reverse-engineers the Charnwood-E Android app and verifies BLE pairing/control, Wi-Fi polling and 21 Home Assistant entities against a live stove.
outcome: Local MQTT/Home Assistant integration for one physically tested wood stove while its onboard controls remain authoritative.
warnings: This controls a real fire. Never use the project as a safety system or justification for unattended operation.
The Aire 300 is the named live target; broader Charnwood E-series compatibility is not established.
Preserve manufacturer operating rules and keep the stove's own controls authoritative.

title: Read and guard-write a Micro-Air EasyStart over BLE
summary: microair-bt derives the OEM BLE protocol and exposes live data plus a guarded, hardware-verified relearn command through an ESPHome proxy.
outcome: Local compressor soft-starter telemetry and a narrow verified configuration write for one exact model.
warnings: SCPT and fault-protection writes are not hardware-verified and remain experimental.
Writes are refused while the compressor runs unless a user overrides the guard; do not bypass this casually.
Bad protection values can damage a mains-powered compressor system.

title: Run a Govee ice maker without its cloud
summary: The Home Assistant integration implements the exact model's 20-byte BLE protocol, reverse-engineered from the Android app, including power, work mode and device-only alarms.
outcome: Cloud-free control plus low-water and tray-full state that the stock cloud path does not need to mediate.
warnings: Do not infer support for other Govee ice makers.
BLE range and single-client contention with the official app must be tested at installation.
Software alarms do not replace the appliance's physical protections or supervision.

title: Use a Roomba 692 through its local MQTT API
summary: roomba-telemetry uses the reverse-engineered local MQTT/TLS interface for live state, schedules, preferences and mission commands, with one physically verified exact model.
outcome: Local vacuum telemetry and control with a pairing-first credential path and a documented cloud-login fallback.
warnings: Broader model support comes partly from community references; the physical validation cited here is for Roomba 692.
Some firmware ignores local pairing and requires the documented cloud credential fallback.
Protect the vacuum's BLID/password and isolate local MQTT traffic.

title: Decode a Wii Nunchuk from a saved I2C capture
exact_models: Wired Wii Nunchuk; capture revision not recorded
summary: REA and sigrok decode the extension controller's initialization, register selection and three six-byte sensor/button reads from a pinned logic capture.
outcome: A reproducible seven-transaction I2C analysis that can guide controller repurposing without claiming the capture's unknown retail revision.
warnings: The capture does not record whether the controller is an official wired unit or a clone; wireless variants use different handshakes.
Use the correct connector, 3.3 V, SDA/SCL pinout and pull-ups; wrong voltage or pinout can damage controller or host.
REA analyzed a saved file. It did not acquire traffic from or validate a live Nunchuk.

title: Inspect an Archer C7 OpenWrt image with REA
summary: REA pins and statically scans the exact OpenWrt sysupgrade artifact with firmware-region tooling, recording its digest and workflow without claiming a physical flash.
outcome: A reproducible firmware-analysis example for signatures and regions, linked to Hackshop's existing Archer C7 device and flash playbook.
warnings: The captured file is a sysupgrade image, not a stock-to-OpenWrt factory image.
Static analysis does not prove bootability, partition semantics, runtime behavior or flash safety.
REA did not flash a physical router; use the separate exact-revision installation and recovery playbook.

title: Recover inverted UART through a MAX3232E capture
summary: REA validates a pinned sigrok capture and shows why DOUT1 inversion is required to recover five Hello world frames instead of plausible but wrong bytes.
outcome: A reusable example of polarity-aware UART decoding across an RS-232 transceiver.
warnings: MAX3232E is a component, not a self-contained consumer device.
RS-232 voltage levels and polarity are not MCU TTL UART; use a proper transceiver and account for inversion.
REA analyzed an existing saved capture rather than acquiring data from live hardware.

title: Analyze saved firmware and signal captures with REA
summary: REA combines evidence capture, firmware extraction/signature workflows and saved signal-recording analysis. Its public showcase is software-only; the hardware-bearing evidence lives in its experiment corpus.
outcome: A repeatable research method for inspecting files and preserving evidence without overstating live-device validation.
warnings: REA's five public showcase cases are software investigations, not hackable-hardware examples.
Saved-file analysis does not acquire from, execute on or prove behavior of physical hardware.
Firmware signatures and decoder output do not establish vulnerabilities, bootability or safe flashing.

title: Reverse-engineer an AC into a menu-bar and glasses UI
summary: Ilter Canberk demonstrated an AC status-bar controller, then ported the same interface to Spectacles with an appliance-anchored Lens Studio overlay.
outcome: A compact desktop controller and an AR control surface shown operating the author's air conditioner.
warnings: No exact DELLA model, protocol, repository, firmware or recovery path is published in the cited posts.
A social video proves an author demonstration, not compatibility or safe repeatability.
Do not conflate this with unrelated TCL or cloud-control projects.

title: Control a 3D home with House Control, Hue and Home Assistant
outcome: A documented path from a simulated 3D floor plan to explicitly linked lights and climate devices, plus optional permission-limited agent access. This enriches the existing apartment example; it is not a new hardware model, a universal reverse-engineering exploit or independent real-device verification.

sources.label: Hackshop setup guide and integration-boundary diagram
Pinned House Control implementation and license notice
Pinned AI Access permissions and privacy

summary: 0xProbabillity's apartment interface now has an inspectable MIT-licensed House Control implementation. Its Three.js floor plan connects through documented integrations including Hue Bridge, Home Assistant and Smart Life/Tuya. Unlinked devices remain simulated; no exact lamp or AC compatibility has been independently verified by Hackshop.
warnings: The repository documents integrations, not blanket model compatibility. Exact hardware models, firmware and Hackshop physical tests remain unknown. A moving Three.js scene does not prove a real device changed state.

Hue Bridge and Home Assistant use local routes; Smart Life/Tuya uses its cloud. The iPhone editions differ. Per the connection guide, Apple Home on Mac is linking/simulated; real Apple Home control occurs on iPhone.

AI Access is optional and may open a tunnel. Anyone holding its private link can exercise enabled permissions; some documented action links can mutate device state. Start read-only, limit scope and duration, never publish the link, and stop it when finished.

Room names, device state and floor plans may be visible to the agent provider and handled by the tunnel provider. Keep sign-ins and tokens private; do not treat a tunnel or a simulated plan as a privacy or safety guarantee.

Begin with a low-risk lamp, retain physical controls and device-specific limits, and verify actual state before permitting climate or whole-home actions. This listing does not connect to or control your home.

Follow the pinned release/build verification instructions; do not bypass operating-system security checks automatically. Code licensing does not by itself grant permission to reuse every creator photo or video.
No Hackshop real-device walkthrough or finished-build photo is available. Our integration diagram is an illustration; no creator media is rehosted.
device_name: House Control for Mac / iPhone with mixed smart-home devices

design_ideas.title: One-room lamp control
design_ideas.description: Start with the bundled simulated plan, then deliberately link one low-risk lamp through Hue or Home Assistant and verify physical state changes in both directions. Keep other devices simulated until individually checked.

design_ideas.title: Scoped agent room interface
design_ideas.description: Explore the interface without hardware first. If agent access is later enabled, start read-only, use narrow permissions and short expiry, and protect the private link like a credential.

title: Expose a Blue Star AC through MCP
device_name: Blue Star air conditioner (exact model undisclosed)
summary: A social demonstration shows a reverse-engineered Blue Star air conditioner exposed through an MCP control surface.
outcome: An agent-facing appliance controller demonstrated against the author's AC.
warnings: The cited post does not publish an exact model, protocol implementation, repository or recovery path.
Treat the MCP layer as an interface demonstration, not evidence that an appliance is safely controllable.
Require explicit confirmation and device readback for consequential HVAC writes.

title: Pair an Apple Watch Ultra 2 with Android
summary: Apple Watch Companion reconstructs native Bluetooth, pairing, activation and IDS protocols. The author's hardware journal records optical camera pairing, activation, a visible watch face and encrypted reconnect on the tested Watch and Android phone.
outcome: An experimental Android companion with native battery observations, selected settings and partial notification and face-management support on one tested device combination.
warnings: Android HAL support is restricted to rooted OnePlus CPH2653. Retained physical evidence covers Ultra 2 Watch7,5 on watchOS 26.2/23S303.
Clean Android Companion builds require undistributed optical firmware inputs and private asset-generation tools; this remains an experimental release candidate.
Calls/audio, Health import, app management and Watch.app parity are incomplete. macOS currently offers discovery and BLE only.
Preserve pairing records. Uninstalling or clearing app data destroys the saved pair; a general Android pair-export/restore path is not documented.
The repository has no declared top-level license, and distribution of firmware-derived assets is an open release gate.

sources.label: Release support and missing build inputs

title: Control Hue bulbs and store schedules over Bluetooth
device_name: Philips Hue White and Color Ambiance bulb
summary: OpenHue is a native macOS BLE controller with published GATT protocol notes. Its author decoded on-bulb alarm storage and verified schedule creation on LCA003 firmware 1.163.1.
outcome: Local power, brightness, color, scenes and timers, including stored schedules that can fire while the Mac is absent.

design_ideas.title: Calendar reminder light
design_ideas.description: Have a local Mac scheduler re-arm the bulb's one-shot schedule for the next meeting. The bulb holds the event once synchronized, but daily repetition requires the host.

design_ideas.title: AI status lamp
design_ideas.description: Map a trusted agent's idle, thinking and ready states to color and brightness. The AI runs on a computer or service; the bulb is its ambient output.

warnings: Stored schedules are physically verified only on LCA003 firmware 1.163.1, are one-shot and need re-arming. Power loss stops the bulb clock until resynchronized.
OpenHue currently supports one connected BLE client per bulb and does not support bridge-joined bulbs; this is an app support limit, not a universal Hue hardware restriction.
Factory reset removes pairing and changes the BLE address. Try discoverable pairing before resetting.
The app is development-signed rather than notarized, and the repository has no declared license.

title: Drive a Hue bulb directly from Python
device_name: Philips Hue White and Color Ambiance E27 1100-lumen bulb
summary: MIT-licensed HueBLE uses Bleak to control Hue's BLE GATT interface, exposing power, brightness, color temperature, color, effects and transitions without a Hue Bridge.
outcome: A local programmable light for timers, calendar reminders and dashboard-linked state, with tested-model and live-state caveats documented.

design_ideas.title: Desk focus timer
design_ideas.description: Use a Python service to change hue through focus and break periods. Read live state after connecting, and keep the timing logic on the host.

design_ideas.title: Dashboard-linked light
design_ideas.description: Connect a calendar or information panel to a local Python BLE service and map a small set of states to color, temperature and brightness.

warnings: Automatic discovery is documented as tested only on LCA006 firmware 1.104.2; other models and effects need their own check.
Call poll_state after connecting before treating default cached values as observed bulb telemetry.
Factory reset changes the Bluetooth address and removes pairing.
Concurrent Zigbee and BLE is documented by HueBLE but requires its specific pairing flow.

title: Control Hue bulbs through Zigbee2MQTT
summary: Zigbee2MQTT documents direct coordinator support for exact Hue bulbs, including brightness, color temperature, applicable color controls, power-on behavior and Hue-specific effects.
outcome: Local MQTT control from calendars, AI agents, information panels or Home Assistant using a supported Zigbee coordinator.
warnings: A supported Zigbee coordinator and running Zigbee2MQTT host are required.
Moving a bulb to another Zigbee network requires removing or resetting its prior network association.
White Ambiance LTA002 has no RGB color; choose a supported color bulb for colored AI state indicators.
Power-on behavior set to off can prevent a wall-switch power cycle from illuminating the bulb.

title: Build calendar and AI lighting with the Hue Bridge API
device_name: Philips Hue Bridge V2 and paired lights
exact_models: Capabilities read from paired bulb resources
summary: Hue's official local REST interface provides bridge discovery, physical link-button authorization, state reads and light commands. Home Assistant adds local push updates on V2 bridges.
outcome: A straightforward local integration for existing Hue owners, with per-light capabilities discovered from the bridge.
warnings: Requires a working bridge and locally authorized application key. Match commands to each bulb's reported capabilities; white-only bulbs cannot display RGB states.

sources.label: Home Assistant Hue local push integration

title: Build a tiny color panel on a $9 T-Display-S3
exact_models: ESP32-S3, 170x320 LCD, 16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM
summary: Manufacturer Arduino, PlatformIO and ESP-IDF examples, factory firmware and BOOT/RST recovery make this inexpensive screen a documented native text-and-image client.
outcome: A small programmable Wi-Fi display for one appointment, countdown, status or remote AI response.

price.note: H569 China $9.04; H577 China $9.54 or US $14.04. Touch variants $12.61-$13.02. Add USB power, cable and enclosure; shipping/tax extra. This MCU renders data from a host or remote AI service.

design_ideas.title: Next appointment countdown
design_ideas.description: Have a trusted calendar service send the next event and minutes remaining over Wi-Fi. The 170x320 screen fits a single event rather than a whole month.

design_ideas.title: AI response tile
design_ideas.description: Show the latest short response or agent state using native text/image rendering. AI inference and private account access stay on a computer or remote service.

design_ideas.title: Desk status panel
design_ideas.description: Display weather, transit or build status refreshed by an HTTP/MQTT service. Use a native screen layout rather than expecting a desktop web browser.

warnings: Match touch versus non-touch variants and GPIO definitions. GPIO15 must enable display power.
Factory firmware and BOOT/RST download mode provide the documented recovery route.
There is no onboard SD slot without an add-on, and this board is not a general-purpose LLM computer.

title: Build a 7-inch calendar or room panel for $36.99
summary: Official Arduino/LVGL examples and factory test firmware provide a repeatable starting point for a large native touchscreen layout.
outcome: An affordable large-screen renderer for calendars, room status and remote AI interfaces.

price.note: Touch SKU27078 only. The $31.99 listing is non-touch SKU30406, a separate variant. Add power/cable, stand or case, and a service supplying calendar or AI data; shipping/tax extra.

design_ideas.title: Kitchen calendar
design_ideas.description: Render a week view with large event text and weather in LVGL. A trusted backend reduces calendar data to the fields the panel needs.

design_ideas.title: Room control panel
design_ideas.description: Combine lights, temperature and a few scene buttons on the 800x480 touch screen, using authenticated Home Assistant or MQTT services on the host.

design_ideas.title: AI briefing screen
design_ideas.description: Show concise responses and image cards from a remote AI endpoint. This ESP32 runs the interface; it does not host a desktop browser or local LLM.

warnings: Match the original touch board to its firmware; 7B is a different 1024x600 device.
Use official test firmware/reflash instructions as the recovery path.
The displayed device price excludes the complete build's power, mounting and backend costs.

title: Make a low-power 4.7-inch e-paper calendar
exact_models: H578 basic / H580 soldered / H716 touch
summary: The manufacturer's ESP32-S3 branch supplies display examples and USB download-mode recovery for this 16 MB flash/8 MB PSRAM e-paper board.
outcome: A grayscale display for periodic calendar, weather, chores or generated briefing images.

price.note: China H578 $38.99, H580 $39.62, H716 $39.99. Add a compatible battery or USB power and frame; a host renders authenticated calendar/AI images. Shipping/tax extra.

design_ideas.title: Daily calendar sheet
design_ideas.description: Render the day's agenda and weather as a 960x540 grayscale bitmap on a host, then fetch it periodically and sleep between updates.

design_ideas.title: AI morning briefing
design_ideas.description: Generate a short briefing remotely and rasterize it into a static grayscale page. Slow, deliberate refreshes suit e-paper better than chat animation.

design_ideas.title: Chores and room noticeboard
design_ideas.description: Show a few tasks or room status changes with occasional full refreshes to limit ghosting.

warnings: Use the esp32s3 branch; classic ESP32 T5 instructions target a different board.
The manufacturer warns against persistent partial refresh. screen_repair may reduce ghosting but is not guaranteed.
Use USB BOOT/RST download mode for recovery.

title: Use a $29.90 magnetic e-paper status tile
summary: CoreInk combines a finished magnetic case, RTC and 390 mAh battery with supported M5Unified/M5GFX libraries and factory Easyloader recovery.
outcome: A compact battery information tile for one appointment, task, room label or short AI summary.

price.note: K048 includes case and 390mAh battery; seller showed 10+ units. Add USB charging/cable and a data service. Its 200x200 screen is a small tile, not a full calendar page. Shipping/tax extra.

design_ideas.title: Next meeting tile
design_ideas.description: Show one meeting name and start time on the 200x200 screen, using the RTC between occasional Wi-Fi updates.

design_ideas.title: Magnetic room label
design_ideas.description: Display occupied/free state, one task or a short summary on a metal surface. Update at least 15 seconds apart as the manufacturer recommends.

warnings: Use M5Unified/M5GFX; the old M5Core-Ink library is deprecated.
The manufacturer recommends at least 15 seconds between refreshes.

title: Jukebox for Alexa: personal MP3s and internet radio
device_name: Amazon Echo with an Alexa AudioPlayer custom skill
summary: A source-checked custom-skill design inspired by the levelsio prompt supplied by a reader. Amazon's AudioPlayer guide and sample provide the starting point; S3 or R2 presigned GET URLs can keep the music bucket private. This is a design guide, not a released Jukebox implementation or a Hackshop-tested Echo build.
outcome: Implementation path: enable AudioPlayer, map voice requests to a personal music library or radio list, issue HTTPS playback URLs, and handle playback events and pause/resume. Library matching, album ordering, shuffle and radio recovery remain application work. Alexa and Amazon cloud services stay in place; no firmware replacement or root access is involved.
warnings: Documentation supports the integration pattern, not this complete implementation. Exact Echo generation, locale and firmware are unknown; no physical playback, long resume, queue continuity or reconnect test is claimed.

The original X link and attribution were supplied by a reader; the post was not independently retrieved. No implementation repository or creator media permission was established. No third-party photo or video is rehosted.

Use a development-stage custom skill on devices registered to the same developer account; this is not Amazon's enterprise private-skill distribution mechanism. Cloud hosting, storage and transfer may incur costs.

Audio URLs, including streams referenced inside playlists, must meet Alexa's HTTPS, trusted-certificate, port and encoding requirements. No named radio station or stream endpoint has been verified for this entry; check availability, region and permitted use before adding one.

Keep the bucket private and grant the skill only the required list/read permissions. Presigned URLs are bearer credentials: never publish or log them. AWS temporary credentials can expire before a requested 12-hour URL lifetime; R2 signing uses its S3 API hostname, not a custom domain.

AudioPlayer tokens are limited to 1024 characters and must not contain customer data. Use opaque identifiers, not music paths or secrets; ENQUEUE requires a matching expectedPreviousToken. A database-free queue is a proposed design, not a validated guarantee.

Test real playback, pause/resume, track changes and radio failures on the target Echo. The simulator does not render AudioPlayer playback; that limitation does not make every simulator error harmless. Use only music and streams you are permitted to play.
